text: A psalm of David. For remembrance.
LORD, do not rebuke me in your anger, or discipline me in your wrath.
For your arrows have pierced me, and your hand has come down hard on me.
There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation; there is no peace in my bones because of my sin.
My guilt has risen over my head; like a heavy burden it weighs me down.
My wounds are foul and festering because of my foolishness.
I am bent over and utterly crushed; all day long I walk about in mourning.
My inmost parts are filled with burning, and there is no soundness in my flesh.

versions.text: My body burns with fever, and there is no soundness in my flesh.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כְסָלַי refers specifically to the loins/inner parts, and נִקְלֶה is a burning or inflammation, not necessarily 'fever' (a diagnostic term not in the text). Rendering the inner body and the burning keeps the image concrete without adding a medical claim.

text: I am worn out and completely broken; I groan from the anguish of my heart.
Lord, all my longing lies open before you; my sighing is not hidden from you.
My heart pounds, my strength fails me, and even the light of my eyes is gone.
My friends and companions keep their distance from my affliction; my relatives stand far off.

versions.text: My friends and companions keep their distance from my affliction; my neighbors stand far off.
versions.explanation: קְרוֹבַי denotes near kin/relatives rather than 'neighbors'; the point is that even close family withdraws, which heightens the isolation of the lament.

text: Those who want my life set their traps; those who seek my ruin speak of destruction, and all day long they plot deceit.
But I am like a deaf man who does not hear, like a mute who does not open his mouth.
I have become like a man who hears nothing, whose mouth offers no reply.
For in you, LORD, I have put my hope; you will answer, Lord my God.
For I said, "Do not let them gloat over me"—for when my foot slips, they boast against me.

versions.text: For I said, "Do not let them gloat over me, or exalt themselves against me when my foot slips."
versions.explanation: The second clause (עָלַי הִגְדִּילוּ) is a statement of what the enemies actually do, not part of the petition. Keeping it as a statement preserves the movement from prayer to reason and reads naturally aloud.

text: For I am ready to fall, and my pain is always with me.
So I confess my guilt; I am troubled by my sin.
My enemies are vigorous and strong; many hate me without cause.
They repay my good with evil; they oppose me for pursuing what is good.
Do not abandon me, LORD; my God, do not be far from me.
Come quickly to help me, my Lord, my salvation.
